correctness.rationale: For every sign orbit, exactly two configurations have uniformly signed nonzero cofactors. The unsigned minor vector is sign invariant; on successful configurations, it exactly determines both barycentric origin weights and Euclidean simplex volume. Gram–Schmidt and spherical covariance yield independent- and common-column determinant moments in arbitrary dimension, and the four-point third moment uses an explicitly evaluated angular correlation. Symbolic exact manipulation and a rigorous rational upper bound for π establish negative centered cubic; standalone finite checks passed. Scope includes required nonzero minors and radial moments.

originality.rationale: The Wendel sign-orbit mechanism and unconditional simplex determinant moments are acknowledged prior art. On inspected evidence the complete origin-conditioned volume first/second moment hierarchy and especially the evaluated four-sphere-vertex third moment with strictly negative centered skewness are not implied by previously published conditional Gaussian weights, volume-small tetrahedral limits, shallow facet laws, or existing unconditional volume tables. First-principle triple-minor integration supplies the new ingredient. Priority remains provisional because the full text of Miles 1971 was inaccessible.
residual_risks: Miles (1971) original full text inaccessible; could contain stronger conditional variants not visible in its abstract and the accessible later unconditional-volume citations.
Other literature on random spherical simplices might encode the same third moment using a different conditioning or signed determinant identity; prior search is extensive but not exhaustive.
The sign-orbit identity is an application of Wendel-type symmetry, not independently novel; originality rests on evaluated conditional moments and third-order structure.
Complete Ruben–Miles (1980) canonical decomposition was also inaccessible and may contain more general moment machinery; only its abstract could be compared.

value.rationale: Origin-contained spherical simplices are a natural geometric conditional population for spherical covering and random convex hulls. Euclidean volume is their central metric invariant; exact mean and dispersion determine conditional size, while the third moment and its strictly negative central sign expose nontrivial distributional asymmetry not determined by lower moments. The three-minor contraction is a substantive, reproducible structural evaluation, and general radial formulas identify sharp moment requirements.
